analysis.title: Weekly Market View: Policy, politics and earnings
key_insights: The CIO Office keeps a defensive and diversified stance across assets, sectors and regions through the next two weeks of central bank meetings, US mid-term elections and Big Tech earnings.

It expects the Fed, ECB and BoJ to hold rates next week after September hikes, and to hike next in December because fuel prices are likely to stay elevated into early next year on refining capacity constraints.

The Fed and ECB are expected to deliver less than the roughly 60bps of hikes priced by money markets over the next 12 months, on the view that easing oil and fuel prices lead to disinflation by H2 2027. 3-7-year DM investment grade bonds are said to offer attractive risk-reward.

The bank expects BoE, Bank of Canada and RBNZ to hike 25bps in the next two weeks. It sees the RBA near the end of its hiking cycle (money markets give 60% odds of a hike on 3 November) and favours AUD corporate bonds for income and FX gains.

Prediction markets strongly favour Democrats winning the House and possibly the Senate on 3 November. A divided government has historically produced the best 12-month equity returns, but a decisive blue wave raises longer-term risks around higher taxes and AI investment and data-centre policy, so the bank stays cautious on risk assets near term.

Consensus expects over 60% y/y Q3 earnings growth for the US tech sector, the biggest jump in over two decades outside the post-COVID rebound. Leadership is concentrated and share-price reactions are more mixed.

The bank closes its EU bank CoCo idea at a 2.0% gain and its US 10-year Treasury idea at a 1.7% gain, citing French and US political risks. It keeps inflation-protected bonds and an Overweight in gold as hedges.

Sector changes: US Healthcare upgraded to Overweight, Communication Services downgraded to Neutral, and profits taken on semiconductors earlier this month before the latest correction. Overweights stay on US tech, materials, and financials in the US, Euro area and Japan.

Big Tech earnings this week point to strong compute demand and continued capex expansion, but the bank expects debt-financed AI capex to rise from about 25% of AI capex in 2026 to about 40% in 2027, raising rate sensitivity and funding risk. It avoids adding to higher-risk tech areas for now.

The bank stays positive on Euro area bank equities and expects Q3 2026 net interest income to grow 1.5-3.0% q/q, led by Spain. French banks are 13% of the Euro area bank index, and French fiscal uncertainty has widened sovereign spreads.

China equities stay a Core holding on cheap valuations and AI localisation. The MSCI China Index has fallen about 20% over the past year on AI capex scepticism, margin compression, heavy share issuance, chip restrictions and a disappointing September stimulus.

The US 10-year yield fell over 17bps to 4.97% on 22 October, its first close below 5% since 23 September and its biggest one-day drop since March 2023, on an AI equity sell-off and Middle East tensions. Earlier this month it hit its highest level in over two decades. September CPI was 3.7% y/y.

French bank bond weakness is described as a repricing of political and fiscal tail risk, not a credit story. Volatility is expected until the April 2027 presidential election, mainly in junior capital, and sovereign rating reviews are the near-term catalyst.

The bank expects a near-term CHF rebound, driven mainly by safe-haven demand from European bond volatility with the France-Germany 10-year spread near 160bps. A USD/CHF break below 0.8130 would strengthen the case, while the SNB's 0% rate and the risk of intervention with EUR/CHF below 0.90 limit the upside.

The bank expects EUR/USD to recover to 1.17-1.18 over 12 months as the Fed hiking cycle peaks by mid-2027. France's fiscal risk constrains near-term gains, and the main tail risk is fiscal stress spilling into bank funding.

risk_factors: Fuel-price-driven inflation could make the Fed, ECB and BoJ more hawkish than expected.
A decisive Democratic sweep could raise taxes and create uncertainty over AI investment and data-centre policy.
Debt-financed AI capex, expected to rise from about 25% in 2026 to about 40% in 2027, raises interest-rate sensitivity and the risk of delayed revenue recognition.
French fiscal stress could widen sovereign spreads and spill over into bank funding, lending and growth, with a possible sovereign downgrade.
Escalating Middle East tensions and possible renewed Iran strikes keep oil elevated.
US-China trade and technology tensions, including sanctions, export curbs and chip restrictions.
Concentrated market leadership and mixed share-price reactions around Big Tech earnings.

vol_and_positioning: Market leadership is concentrated and share-price reactions to tech earnings are more mixed, raising the risk of volatility and sector divergence.

Proprietary diversity indicators show investor diversity has normalised across asset classes. The EUR/USD fractal dimension is 1.49 (low to mid), and no asset class is below the 1.25 reversal-risk threshold.
Stated technical levels: S&P 500 spot 7,663 with support 7,572 and resistance 7,800. WTI at 99.5, with support 87.4 and resistance 111.0. Gold at 4,025.
geopolitical: President Trump hinted at restarting Iran strikes after the mid-term election.
The US sanctioned five Chinese firms over alleged AI trade-secret theft.
Houthis carried out fresh attacks on Saudi energy, airport and military targets.
China threatened retaliation if the UK raises tariffs on Chinese EVs, and imposed export curbs on drones and machinery.
Middle East tensions are escalating and keeping oil prices elevated.
France's fiscal and political risks run up to the April 2027 presidential election, with sovereign credit rating reviews upcoming.

tension_points.bull_case: An opposition sweep has historically delivered the best 12-month equity returns among all scenarios, partly because of policy gridlock.
tension_points.bear_case: A decisive Democratic blue wave could raise longer-term risks of higher taxes and uncertainty over policy towards AI investment and data centres.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A decisive Democratic win in both the House and Senate on 3 November.

tension_points.bull_case: Tech earnings show strong compute demand and continued capex expansion, and improving AI monetisation should strengthen operating cash flows.
tension_points.bear_case: Debt-financed AI capex is expected to rise from about 25% to about 40%, raising rate sensitivity, and deployment delays could postpone revenue while financing costs continue.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Next week's Big Tech earnings showing weaker capex guidance, funding or AI monetisation trends.

tension_points.theme: Euro area bank equities and French risk
tension_points.bull_case: Resilient earnings, capital returns, eased P/B valuations and strong capital buffers with ECB tools limit system-wide stress.
tension_points.bear_case: French fiscal uncertainty widens sovereign spreads, pressuring banks' bond holdings and funding costs, and a sovereign downgrade could trigger bank downgrades.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A French sovereign downgrade at the upcoming rating reviews.
